correctness.limitations: u>v>0 are fixed and walls suppress outward jumps without resetting orientation. Only stationary distributions are considered. The boundary fraction is total macroscopic atomic weight, not the single-wall-site probability, a heat capacity, or a finite-size derivative. No general dynamics or other scaling assertion follows.
correctness.rationale: Reflection and the zero total current imply rho even, s odd, and w(ρ_{i+1}−ρ_i)=δ(s_i+s_{i+1}) with w=u+v. Subtracting orientation balances and eliminating ρ gives the stated recurrence, so s=A sinh(ki), ρ=B+AH cosh(ki) and 4uv sinh²(k/2)=δ²+αw. At the right wall the plus-current identity becomes j⁺=δB/2−(Aα/2)cosh(k(L−1/2))/sinh(k/2)=αs_L. The half-angle identity yields B/A=(α/δ)cosh(k(L+1/2))/sinh(k/2), the stated boundary coefficient. Normalization is a geometric sum. In the critical window z→u/v and H→1: the normalized constant term gives the bulk Riemann sum and each of the two geometric terms gives an endpoint atom with uniform summable inward decay. The geometric component has zero rescaled interior density for any sequence bounded macroscopically away from the walls. At a fixed inward index j, s and ρ have the same limiting value, so only the outward orientation contributes. This works also at c=0, when the constant component has zero mass. The log derivative on c>0 is y/(1+y)² with y=2c/δ, with unique maximum 1/4 at y=1; its c=0 value is a continuous extension only.

originality.rationale: The exact finite model and its transfer matrix, boundary accumulation, and the scale δ/(2L) are covered by Santra. Continuum sticky-wall balance also covers the form of the macroscopic mixture and the corresponding dimensionless response. The distinct claim is the rigorous two-scale stationary match in this thermal lattice: exact normalization and orientation of a fixed-lattice-spacing geometric profile, simultaneously with the interior and atomic limits and no missing mass. The reference's unexpanded matrix powers require extracting the modes, matching their wall coefficient and controlling normalization in a joint size/flip limit; its finite-site numerical slopes and persistence-length estimate do not perform that analysis.
residual_risks: An earlier expansion of the exact same transfer solution, or a stronger stationary fluid-limit theorem with a lattice boundary-layer estimate, may cover the match. The prior existence of the exact transfer solution is a material overlap, not evidence for novelty of the finite formula.
No global literature priority claim; the precise result compared is the fixed-site, finite-temperature geometric layer matched to the macroscopic limit.

value.rationale: The distinction between macroscopic wall accumulation and microscopic occupancy of an actual lattice site is motivated by the primary work's finite-site measurements. The exact normalized profile tells how the atom is distributed over sites and which orientation carries it while the size and persistence length compete. Neither the continuum shape nor the crossover scale alone answers how many near-wall sites carry that mass.
